# deed_entity_override (Resource)

An **override** of an entity that other sources own (a GitHub repository, a UniFi client, a HallPass server): display name, icon, owner, labels, … and spec values, written to the project's `overrides` source (layer `override`, above declarations and imports) **without declaring the entity**.

- Labels and annotations merge per key, `links` and `tags` as unions; what the override does not set keeps coming from the sources.
- State is read only from the override (`GET /entities/{id}/declarations/overrides`), so other sources' values never cause a diff. Destroying it removes only the override.
- An override never keeps an entity alive. When the last source lets go, the entity is gone and the override reads as removed: Terraform plans to create it again, and the apply fails clearly until a source describes the entity again.

Requires Deed 0.7.0 or later and a project `admin` token. For the same labels on many entities, use `deed_label_rule`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A repository the GitHub connector imports: a friendlier name, an owner and a label, without declaring it.
resource "deed_entity_override" "app_repo" {
  project      = "infra"
  kind         = "repository"
  name         = "example-org-app"
  display_name = "App"
  owner        = "platform"
  labels       = { tier = "core" }
}

# By entity ID, correcting an imported spec value.
resource "deed_entity_override" "nas" {
  entity_id = "ent_01h0000000000000000000000a"
  icon      = "simple-icons:synology"
  spec      = jsonencode({ os = "DSM 7.2" })
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `annotations` (Map of String) Annotations (at most 64; values up to 4096 bytes): free-form notes that are not used for filtering.
- `description` (String) Description (Markdown).
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name.
- `entity_id` (String) The entity to override, by ID. Set either `entity_id`, or `project`, `kind` and `name`. Changing it forces a new resource.
- `environment` (String) Environment slug, e.g. `production` or `homelab`.
- `icon` (String) Icon as `pack:name` (`tabler`, `simple-icons`, `thesvg` or `custom`), e.g. `simple-icons:proxmox`.
- `kind` (String) Kind of the entity to override. Changing it forces a new resource.
- `labels` (Map of String) Labels (at most 64; values up to 256 bytes) used for filtering and grouping. Keys that look like secrets are refused by Deed.
- `lifecycle_stage` (String) Lifecycle stage: `planned`, `active`, `deprecated` or `retired`.
- `links` (Attributes List) Typed external links (at most 32), e.g. the repository, a dashboard or the runbook. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--links))
- `name` (String) Name of the entity to override (aliases work too). Changing it forces a new resource.
- `owner` (String) Owning group: a `group` entity ID or name.
- `project` (String) Project of the entity to override (with `kind` and `name`). Changing it forces a new resource.
- `spec` (String) Kind-specific properties as a JSON object string (use `jsonencode`). Deed validates it server-side against the kind's storage schema (JSON Schema 2020-12), so the provider does not model custom-kind properties as attributes. Deed stores the document re-encoded (sorted keys, compact); the value is compared semantically, so that never causes a diff (reformatting the document in the configuration shows one in-place update that changes nothing in Deed). Values whose keys look like secrets must be secret references (`{ secretRef = { store = "vault", key = "…" } }`).
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags (at most 64, each 1–64 bytes).
- `version_channel` (String) Release channel, e.g. `stable`.
- `version_declared` (String) Declared version of the software, e.g. `1.27.3`.
- `version_policy` (String) Version policy, e.g. `pinned` or `latest-minor`.
- `version_product` (String) Product the version refers to (for upstream release tracking).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Entity ID (`ent_…`) of the overridden entity.
- `project_id` (String) Project ID (`prj_…`).

<a id="nestedatt--links"></a>
### Nested Schema for `links`

Required:

- `type` (String) `repository`, `dashboard`, `logs`, `docs`, `runbook`, `metrics`, `alerts`, `ticket` or `other`.
- `url` (String) Absolute `https://` URL (`http://` only when the project allows http links).

Optional:

- `title` (String) Link title.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By entity ID, or <project>/<kind>/<name>.
terraform import deed_entity_override.app_repo infra/repository/example-org-app
```
